title: Route Performance History Comparison: Two GPX
description: Compare two GPX efforts on a route with Route Performance History Comparison — distance, pace, elevation and heart rate, file versus file. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, last month's 10.02 km in 52:30 (5:14.4/km) against today's 10.05 km in 50:12 (4:59.7/km) is 14.7 seconds per kilometre faster — a 4.67% improvement the comparison computes, not vibes.
quick_answer: The Route Performance History Comparison loads two GPX files — an earlier effort and a later one — and compares distance, time, average pace, elevation gain and average heart rate where recorded. Your files never leave the browser; the comparison is computed locally from the two recordings you choose.

March: 10.02 km, 52:30 → 314.4 s/km (5:14.4). April: 10.05 km, 50:12 → 299.7 s/km (4:59.7). Difference: 14.7 s/km, 4.67% faster — at similar heart rate, that is fitness; at much higher heart rate, that is effort. The comparison shows both, because one without the other misleads.

If the two files differ by 400 m, they are not the same route or one GPS cut a corner. Compare paces only when distances roughly agree — the tool shows both distances precisely so this check is yours to make.

popular_table.note: Both files must contain the fields being compared. Missing heart rate or elevation in one file narrows the comparison to what both honestly hold.

faq: Do the files need to be the same route?
The comparison works on any pair, but it means something only for the same course in the same direction. Different routes compare numbers; same routes compare performances.
One file has no heart rate.
Then heart-rate rows compare as absent — the rest of the comparison stands. Many watches record HR only with a strap or optical sensor enabled.
Files with pauses contain both stories. The comparison uses the file's recorded spans consistently for both efforts — consistency matters more than the choice.
Elevation gain differs between my watch and this.
Gain algorithms differ (thresholds smooth small bumps differently). Comparing two files under one algorithm here is fairer than comparing two devices' own summaries.
GPS variance on identical routes runs 1–2% normally. Paces computed per-file remain comparable; treat sub-1% pace differences as noise.
Can it compare a plan against an effort?
A route file (plan) against a track (effort) compares distance and elevation only — no times exist in a plan. Still useful for course-checking.
Nowhere but your files. There is no account and no stored history — your archive is your history, which is why the comparison asks for two files each time.
